name: Bau Sau
scriptText: Bau Sau is a wetland of international importance, recognized under the Ramsar Convention. This place is considered the heart of the Nam Cat Tien ecosystem. This vast wetland is the natural home of hundreds of Siamese crocodiles, a rare freshwater crocodile species once believed to be extinct. Visiting here, you will admire pristine scenery reminiscent of an ink wash painting, and experience rowing a boat amidst the wetland where crocodiles live in their natural habitat.

name: Ancient Tung Tree
scriptText: This is a giant tree more than four hundred years old, soaring in height. The most distinctive feature of the Tung tree is its massive, exposed buttress root system that spreads wide and grips tightly into the earth, forming magnificent natural buttresses. To completely encircle the base of this tree requires the joined hands of about twenty adults.

name: Uncle Dong's Redwood Tree
scriptText: This is an ancient tree belonging to the rare red wood species, more than seven hundred years old. The name Uncle Dong's Redwood Tree was given to commemorate the visit of the late Prime Minister Pham Van Dong to the park and his counsel on the conservation of forest resources in the year nineteen eighty-eight. The trunk is massive, with its canopy shading an entire corner of the pristine primary forest.

name: Loc Giao Banyan Tree
scriptText: This is one of the wondrous masterpieces of nature in Cat Tien. The tree has an extraordinarily unique shape, formed by hundreds of clustered roots and trunks intertwining and clinging tightly around a former host tree. The Loc Giao Banyan Tree symbolizes the fierce, resilient, and enduring vitality of tropical forest vegetation.

name: Hundred-Trunk Ficus Tree
scriptText: This is a cluster of ancient ficus trees growing right beside a cool stream. Over hundreds of years of growth, the branches and aerial roots of the tree have dropped down, penetrating deeply into the ground and the water's surface. They form an intricate, winding, and secluded network of trunks, resembling a mystical labyrinth.

name: Da Co Crape Myrtle Forest
scriptText: This is a trail filled with the blossoms of the hairy crape myrtle. During the dry season, particularly from March to May every year, the entire forest sheds its leaves simultaneously and dons a brilliant purple cloak. That romantic and poetic scenery is completely different from the year-round lush green of the primeval forest.

name: Thac Troi Waterfall
scriptText: Thac Troi, also known as Thac Dung, is a majestic waterfall winding through undulating basalt rock fields in the midst of the vast green forest. The waterfall cascades down with white frothing spray year-round, creating mystical veils of water mist. On beautiful sunny days, sunlight pierces through the mist, creating vibrant rainbows. That is why this place is called Thac Troi, or Heaven Waterfall.

name: Ben Cu Rapids
scriptText: Ben Cu Rapids is located not far from the park headquarters. Here, a section of the Dong Nai River narrows, its torrent rushing and weaving through large, undulating rocky rapids. Ben Cu possesses a wild and rustic beauty, serving as an ideal stopover for you to rest and listen to the murmuring sound of flowing water harmonizing with the songs of forest birds.

name: Mo Vet Waterfall
scriptText: The current here flows past rock banks with a distinctive shape, curving sharply like a parrot's beak. Unlike the ferocious demeanor of Thac Troi, Mo Vet Waterfall possesses a gentle and tranquil beauty, with the canopies of ancient forest trees casting shadows over the clear blue water.

name: Night Wildlife Watching Area
scriptText: This is one of the unique experiences, and the only one of its kind in Vietnam. You will sit in specialized open-top vehicles and accompany a guide deep into the forest amidst the quiet of the night. Under specialized spotlights, you will directly observe the nocturnal wildlife of animals such as sambar deer, barking deer, civets, and porcupines foraging for food.

name: Cat Tien Nature Museum
scriptText: The museum is located right near the administrative headquarters. It preserves and displays thousands of vivid specimens of rare indigenous wildlife, insects, plants, and fungi. This is an ideal starting point, providing you with a scientific overview of the park's biodiversity.

name: Wildlife Rescue Center
scriptText: This is the place that receives, provides medical treatment, and gives special care to individual wild animals, especially Asian black bears and sun bears, that have been injured by illegal poaching and trafficking. Here, you will learn humane rescue stories and the work of rehabilitating wild behaviors before releasing the animals back into nature.

name: Dao Tien Primate Rescue Station
scriptText: Dao Tien is an isolated forest island surrounded by the river, dedicated to the conservation of rare primates such as yellow-cheeked gibbons and silvered langurs. A semi-wild environment has been established here to train individual primates to readapt to natural life before being fully released into the deep forest.

name: Cat Tien Archaeological Site
scriptText: Stretching along the Dong Nai River, this is an ancient religious sanctuary bearing architectural traces dating from the fourth to the eighth century. The relic site was profoundly influenced by the Hindu culture of the ancient kingdom of Funan. Archaeologists have discovered numerous temples and towers, along with ritual ablution spouts, including Yonis and Lingas made of quartz, gold, and ceramics, possessing priceless historical value.

name: Ta Lai Ethnic Cultural Village
scriptText: Located in the buffer zone of the national park, Ta Lai village has long been home to the Ma and S'tieng ethnic minority communities. Coming here, you will be welcomed at a traditional Longhouse, savor unique rustic dishes, watch artisans hand-weaving brocade, and listen to the deep, resonant echoes of the Central Highlands gongs.
